title: You hate what you see in the mirror… but heaven disagrees.
paragraphs: You hate what you see in the mirror… but heaven disagrees.
“I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made; your works are wonderful, I know that full well.” — Psalm 139:14
Let that hit.

Not tolerated.
Not barely acceptable.
Wonderfully made.
But here’s the tension…

You remember your failures.
Your hidden habits.
The version of you nobody applauds.
So how can that person be “wonderful”?
But here’s what we miss…

David didn’t say, “I feel wonderful.”
He said, “I am made wonderful.”
There’s a difference.

Your worth was not handcrafted by your performance.
It was spoken into you by your Creator.

And yes—sin distorts.
Sin stains.
Sin lies.
But it does not rewrite the original design of God over your life.
That’s why Jesus came.

Not to agree with your shame.
But to break it.

At the cross, He didn’t say, “Fix yourself first.”
He said, “It is finished.”
Meaning:

Your value is not up for debate.
Your identity is not canceled by your past.
Your story is not over.

So when you look in the mirror again—
don’t just see what you’ve done.
See what God has declared.

And if your heart whispers, “I’m not enough…”
answer it with Scripture.
“I am fearfully and wonderfully made.”
Say it again.
Until your soul believes what heaven already knows.
